answer_1.quote: We ask LLMs to write a short literature review c_g_i according to the research topic... We then ask LLMs to complete three tasks based on the collected dataset: generating references, writing an abstract, and writing a complete literature review based on a given topic.
answer_1.outputs: References, abstracts, and full literature reviews

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the generated results from multiple dimensions, including the presence of hallucinations in the references, as well as the semantic coverage and factual consistency of the generated abstract and literature review compared to the human-written context... We use ROUGE, KPR, NLI models, semantic similarity, precision, overlap rate, and title search rate.

answer_3.quote: LLMs-as-judges has become more common. So, for the Abstract Writing task, we employ TRUE, along with GPT-4o as NLI models for evaluating factual consistency in context.

answer_4.quote: These references were assessed by three annotators and the final manual results were obtained by majority vote... The human evaluations conducted in this study were carried out by members of the research team.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators judged whether each generated reference corresponded to a real article (i.e., hallucination detection).
